## Existing project / technology non-negotiables

- **First audit the user-supplied, already working frontend**: Public pages, Authentication, Onboarding, shared design tokens, App Shell, assets, modules, mock services and Ahmed's existing files. Work in that SAME codebase. Never create another frontend, never replace the public website, and never delete another teammate's modules.
- Use **HTML5 + CSS3 + Vanilla JavaScript ES6+** and ES Modules. No React, Vue, Angular, Vite, TypeScript, Razor, backend, or new frontend framework. Bootstrap only if already present and not visually disruptive.
- Match the provided per-page UI screenshot as closely as reasonably possible in coordinates, spacing, typography, colors, layout proportions, component sizes, iconography and exact text. Reuse the real official logo/illustrations. Render **actual semantic HTML controls**, not a flat screenshot background. When a decorative source asset is absent, transparently state the fidelity limit.
- Preserve shared desktop Sidebar + Topbar + mobile navigation from Mostafa; make active nav state accurate. Import existing `tokens.css`, typography, reset, forms, buttons and shared feedback; do not duplicate these wholesale in page CSS.
- Always scope data queries to `workspaceId`; for project pages also `projectId`. Validate URL params and handle absent/invalid context with a visible Not Found / Access Denied state. Preserve context in cross-links. Do not treat mock client-side permissions as security.
- Only simulate frontend operations. Do not claim real persistence, email sending or authorization. No passwords/tokens in storage. Use consistent mock data shared across Workspaces/Projects, so counters, lists and progress agree after changes. Keep sensitive info out of browser storage. Use `textContent` or safe DOM construction, not unsafe user-input HTML injection.
- Handle default, loading, empty, error, denied, success, mobile states. Real UI interactions; no dead buttons, browser `alert()` or `confirm()`. Route to existing teammate pages when appropriate; do not reimplement Kanban, Gantt, Reports, Client Portal or Auth.
- Semantic accessible HTML: meaningful labels, native buttons, correct input types, keyboard focus, `aria-invalid`/linked errors, dialog focus management, adequate contrast, reduced motion, touch targets and no horizontal scroll on 360px devices.
- **Clean code is mandatory**: 4-space indentation unless existing consistent standard, one HTML element/structured block per line, one CSS property per line, one CSS selector block at a time, blank lines between logical sections and functions, descriptive names, small single-purpose JS functions, event listeners instead of inline `onclick`, reusable modules not copy-pasted page logic. NO one-line spaghetti source, no minified source, no duplicated CSS, no huge monolithic script, no emojis in UI.
- Run the actual project from a local HTTP server; never assume ES Modules / fetched fragments work from `file://`. Fix relative paths after any move. Re-test existing Public/Auth/Onboarding routes after changes.

## UI states and acceptance scenarios

- **Unchanged form:** ensure page renders and user can identify this state.
- **Unsaved modifications:** ensure page renders and user can identify this state.
- **Inline validation:** ensure page renders and user can identify this state.
- **Save demo success:** ensure page renders and user can identify this state.
- **Read-only Member/Viewer:** ensure page renders and user can identify this state.
- **Archive confirmation:** ensure page renders and user can identify this state.
- **Workspace not found:** ensure page renders and user can identify this state.

Additional mandatory scenarios:

- **Permission:** authorized actor can perform permitted edits; an unauthorized actor sees disabled/read-only controls or the shared access-denied screen. Authorization in JavaScript is a demo only and must not be called secure.
- **Navigation:** all internal links and dropdown choices preserve workspace/project context, handle invalid IDs, and do not navigate to nonexistent pages.
- **Form feedback:** no browser `alert()`/`confirm()`; use existing inline errors, toasts and modal confirmation.
- **Resilience:** loading, zero data and empty filter results do not crash; results reflect the same shared data source as Overview and Projects List.

## Specific product constraints

- Workspace settings is not My Profile or Account Preferences.
- Owner/Admin only edit where permitted; Viewer sees read-only or access denied.
- Avoid irreversible delete without backend; demo archive only with clear label.

Owner/Admin/Member/Viewer role semantics must be consistent throughout Ahmed's workspace and project pages. No self-escalation, last-owner deletion, cross-workspace member leak or unsafe rendering.

## Code organization, quality and review requirements

- One meaningful responsibility per JS function. Example functions: `getPageContext()`, `loadPageData()`, `renderWorkspaceSettings()`, `handlePrimaryAction()`, `showFieldError()`, `initializePage()`; implement only the ones needed.
- In HTML use proper indentation, blank lines between header/sidebar/main/forms/footer sections; never write an entire DOM subtree on one line.
- In CSS group page sections with section headers, one declaration per line and blank lines between selector blocks. Use shared tokens rather than scattered repeated colors.
- In JS use ES Module imports, `addEventListener`, clear named handlers, early returns, try/catch/finally where asynchronous actions are simulated, and no inline event attributes.
- Scope selectors by page root to avoid accidental side effects on Public/Auth/Onboarding.
- No duplicate page-level Sidebar/Topbar CSS. Reuse the existing shared shell.
- No false security promises, fake invitation emails, fake subscriptions, emojis, or non-working CTAs.
